newsitem.title: UK: China to buy 150,000 T copper in 1997 - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: China to buy 150,000 T copper in 1997 - Macquarie.

text.p: China will import about 150,000 tonnes of copper this year to make up a shortfall, but that will not be enough to spark a rally in prices, broker Macquarie Equities said in a commentary on Monday.
Some forecasts have put the Chinese import requirement for refined copper as high as 400,000 tonnes in 1997, which would fuel a bull market late in the year.
"Our analysis of Chinese supply and demand suggests that this is unlikely to be the case," Macquarie said.
In fact, in the first half of the year China was a small net exporter of copper cathode by 5,000 tonnes. There has been, however, strong buying of concentrate, scrap and semis, it said.
"Consequently, large scale buying of refined copper is not required to meet demand needs in the near term," the broker said.
Macquarie pegged 1997 consumption up 60,000 tonnes at 1.35 million tonnes and production up 81,000 tonnes at 1.2 million tonnes, leaving a shortfall of 150,000 tonnes.
The forecast shortfall is 21,000 tonnes less than 1996, it said.
China's strategic stockpile has no immediate need to buy metal and can pick and choose when to do so, the commentary said.
"The indications we have from China are that it will only buy when prices are below $1.00 per lb ($2,200 per tonne)," it added.
Three months London Metal Exchange prices sank to $2,162 per tonne on Monday morning.
